title: 3d rendered  looks different, when using transparent image
content:
hi ,

CLO giving this type of results when using opacity map. Left side is 3d view window and right side is 3d rendered window, looks different in both the windows.. I am using a transparent image in opacity map. I also used (tried) online PBR textures but all gives different in folding side. although when i am not using transparent map is goes well. 

Please suggest.![2781d73735174d3fba0ee87365749933](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202508/c04f3d42ceba4e49aa1f9aadce561214/images/2781d73735174d3fba0ee87365749933image.png)

### Community Post Comments:


Comment 2: please help on this my .png files having transparency, not properly shown in .glb file whereas in 3d rendered image it is perfectly shown.
Reply 1: Where are you viewing this GLB file? Does it look fine when imported into CLO? Please note that we do not receive notifications about a new reply unless it is under one of the comments we already left, therefore we are unlikely to catch the reply swiftly.

Comment 3: I DID THAT for opacity map but transparent png files gives different result in .glb files whereas it is perfect in 3d rendered image

Comment 4: Hi Melody,Please look at the attached screenshot of opacity map.Yes, Quality render have the same results.
Reply 1: The image looks completely white or at least very low contrast and light in this dimension, only black parts will become transparent. Please check out this tutorial: https://connect.clo-set.com/community/post/c04f3d42ceba4e49aa1f9aadce561214

Comment 5: Hi Melody,In left side image the result comes with back image, if i am using .png with transparency.yes png format have some issues. Quality render have same results.
Reply 1: Is the image you're using for the opacity map a black and white image? Anything that is black will become transparent. Could you share a screenshot of the Property Editor, please?

Comment 6: Hi, sorry, I am a bit lost here. What are you trying to achieve and what looks wrong about the outcome? The 3D window is not the best measure of the output, but always the render window. E.g. there is an issue with certain PNGs that have an alpha layer, even if there is no active transparency in the image itself. How does the 3D window look when you turn on Quality Render?
content_description: This webpage aims to provide guidance and solutions for users experiencing discrepancies between 3D view and rendered output when using opacity maps in CLO software.

title: Stiching/Thread  shadow
content:
![d91b01b2f2554e55b2f5e9d625a56991](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202507/cf77b67b38eb43fb8d85d721fd773781/images/d91b01b2f2554e55b2f5e9d625a56991image.png)Hello Everyone,

Please suggest

3d Rendered image showing shadow effect.

original image below is desired requirement. Please suggest how can we achieve?

![d7e24801570a48a49ed21d669e3e8e05](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202507/cf77b67b38eb43fb8d85d721fd773781/images/d7e24801570a48a49ed21d669e3e8e05IMG20250731120428.jpg)

Regards,

nk

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi,I tried and successful with edited thread texture shadow in PS. IT WORKS.👍🏻Thanks!

Comment 2: Hi. It possibly may also help if you remove the Normal Map from the Sewing where the seam is sewn together

Comment 3: hI lUCILE,Thanks for connectingIt is already off, this option of 3d , uncheck or not is doing nothing for me (myside).
Reply 1: Hi! On your screenshot, is it 2 patterns sewn together and then a topstitch on the seamline or is it just a topstitch on an internal line?If it's the first option, then you can use the Edit Sewing tool, select the sewing line and delete the normal map in the Property Editor.

Comment 4: Hi, please untick the '3D' option in the Property Editor of your top stitch and it should remove the shadow.
content_description: "Explore techniques and suggestions for achieving realistic shadow effects in 3D rendered images."

title: Clo x Coach contest
content:
Is it okay for one of the uploaded 'renders' of the three submitted picture is a breakdown of the bag (pockets and all) with some text about the Design Concept and Research?

![d6790db9d3c04c5ba4f82bb64ad4693f](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202507/6bf75d3dafd4404ea1cd52d9db4f1ec8/images/d6790db9d3c04c5ba4f82bb64ad4693fdownload%20%2892%29.jpeg)It would be something like this (this is an image I found online) with the bag compartments 'expanded' and spread out so you could see it in detail. With a blurb of the design concept, research and reasoning?

If not where can I put this information?

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Yes! That would be great as it helps show your process 🙂
Reply 1: hello love, unfortunately I couldnt participate as my clo file got corrupted and I couldn't recover anything- I'm incredibly heartbroken over it but ill live. I would like to know if we are still allowed to post on social media as I had created an entire collection with research and such?
Reply 2: oh no! We would definitely not stop you from posting your own work though. And please tag us. We love seeing CLO Creations!
content_description: This web page aims to clarify whether including a detailed breakdown render of a bag's compartments, alongside a description of the design concept and research, is permissible within submitted project materials.
